cases.visibleGeometry: Several small rounded highs occur across a gently sloping surface; a larger irregular oval high near the lower centre has adjacent branching rough texture. A faint diagonal band crosses the scene.
cases.alternatives: Rock outcrops, residual boulders, erosion, vegetation-related ground classification, or a track could explain these forms.
cases.supportLimits: The oval and rough branching area include conspicuous interpolated cells; boundaries are less reliable there. Most surrounding surface is measured.

candidates.feature: Irregular oval high with adjacent branching texture
candidates.nextCheck: Compare raw ground returns and nearby imagery to separate rock or erosion from modeled form.

cases.visibleGeometry: Dense, nearly horizontal parallel ridges cover most of the square. A small isolated rounded high appears near the upper right; a sharper curving edge borders the lower right.
cases.alternatives: Regular ridges suggest cultivation or land management. The isolated high could be a boulder, vegetation artifact, or spoil; the edge may be a field or track boundary.
cases.supportLimits: Mostly measured cells, with sparse interpolation, including scattered cells around the lower irregular area. The small high is principally measured.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw returns and aerial context for a boulder or modern object.

cases.visibleGeometry: Three long, roughly north-south, slightly wavering linear breaks cross a mostly smooth surface. A few small isolated bumps occur, without a clear grouped arrangement.
cases.alternatives: Field boundaries, drainage, tracks, or erosion fit the lineaments. Small bumps may be rocks or vegetation-related artifacts.
cases.supportLimits: Lines coincide partly with narrow interpolated strips; the surrounding terrain is largely measured. Their exact profiles need raw-return checks.

cases.visibleGeometry: Curving linear edges outline a broad smooth area. Near the upper-left centre is a cluster of short irregular ridges and hollows, including a small squared-looking bend. Other isolated rough patches occur farther right.
cases.alternatives: The cluster may be rock, erosion, vegetation/classification gaps, or disturbed ground; the broader lines may be tracks or field boundaries.
cases.supportLimits: The central cluster has many interpolated cells, especially along the apparent bends, so its geometry is uncertain. The surrounding smoother ground is mostly measured.

candidates.feature: Cluster of short ridges and hollows
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw ground returns and independent aerial imagery before interpreting the apparent bends.

cases.visibleGeometry: Fine parallel ridges span nearly the entire square, crossed by a broad sinuous low swale from lower left toward upper right. A curved edge lies near the bottom.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation texture and natural drainage or erosion explain the visible pattern; the bottom edge may be a track or field margin.
cases.supportLimits: Measured cells dominate, but scattered interpolation is widespread. Fine ridge detail may be sensitive to processing and should not be treated as a precise profile.

cases.visibleGeometry: Mostly smooth ground contains an isolated rounded high near the upper left, several smaller points along a faint north-south line near the centre, and a textured field corner at upper right.
cases.alternatives: The high may be a boulder, tree-related artifact, or spoil. The central line and field corner suggest tracks or cultivation boundaries.
cases.supportLimits: Ground is overwhelmingly measured; only sparse interpolation around the field corner and edges. The isolated high is well supported in the model, though its origin is unknown.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw returns and aerial imagery to identify surface material or vegetation.

cases.visibleGeometry: Broad smooth undulations cross the central and right area. Closely spaced curving parallel ridges occupy the left edge beside a straight north-south margin. A narrow irregular spike appears near the lower right centre.
cases.alternatives: Contour cultivation or terracing likely explains the left ridges. The broad forms resemble natural drainage and slope variation; the spike may be vegetation or classification noise.
cases.supportLimits: Most cells are measured, with localized interpolation around the spike and scattered patches. Its sharp profile is unreliable.

cases.visibleGeometry: Only the left and lower-left part contains terrain. A steep curved boundary meets a broad dark area; narrow parallel breaks and rough patches run along that margin. A small irregular cluster of bumps lies just left of it.
cases.alternatives: The edge and nearby roughness may be a data or mask boundary, erosion, rocks, or classification effects. There is no clear isolated arrangement away from it.
cases.supportLimits: A large portion is missing. Interpolation is concentrated near the edge and rough patches; apparent edge geometry should not be interpreted as a ground feature.

cases.visibleGeometry: A faint sinuous line runs roughly north-south through otherwise smooth ground. Several isolated bumps align near its upper half. A small rectangular raised outline with an uneven interior appears near the bottom centre.
cases.alternatives: The bumps may be rocks or vegetation artifacts; the line may be a track or drainage. The rectangle could be a recent structure, enclosure, or ground-model artifact.
cases.supportLimits: Most ground is measured. The rectangle contains a concentrated interpolated patch, limiting confidence in its interior and edges.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect raw returns and aerial imagery for a recent structure or classification gap.

cases.visibleGeometry: Regular diagonal parallel ridges cover the square. A prominent curved linear bank or cut runs from lower left toward the top, and another broad parallel edge lies near the lower right.
cases.alternatives: Cultivation rows and field or track boundaries explain the regular texture and lines. No localized discrete form stands out.
cases.supportLimits: Nearly all cells are measured; small interpolation flecks occur along the main line and elsewhere. Ridge profiles are still model-derived.

cases.visibleGeometry: Interlocking broad highs and narrow sinuous lows create an irregular dissected surface. A comparatively smooth tongue-shaped area extends from the centre toward the lower right, edged by shallow curved breaks.
cases.alternatives: Natural drainage and erosion, rock exposures, tracks, or field edges could form the breaks. The smooth tongue may reflect different land use or ground classification.
cases.supportLimits: Scattered interpolation is dense on rough highs and along some linear breaks. The apparent tongue edge partly follows interpolated bands, so continuity is uncertain.

candidates.feature: Smooth tongue with curved marginal break
candidates.nextCheck: Check raw returns across the edge and independent imagery for drainage or field use.

cases.visibleGeometry: Long nearly north-south narrow breaks divide three strips with contrasting surface texture. The middle strip is rougher; the right strip is smoother with faint parallel lines. No compact coherent feature is apparent.
cases.alternatives: Field boundaries, cultivation, tracks, drainage, or vegetation coverage could explain the striping and texture change.
cases.supportLimits: The strongest breaks coincide with narrow interpolated bands; most strip interiors are measured. Exact bank or ditch profiles are uncertain.

cases.visibleGeometry: A compact cluster of sharply irregular highs and clefts lies left of centre, with a smaller isolated bump below it. A faint curved line passes immediately to its right across otherwise smooth terrain.
cases.alternatives: Exposed rock, boulders, rubble, vegetation-related classification, or recent disturbance could explain the cluster; the line may be a track.
cases.supportLimits: The cluster coincides with substantial interpolation, while the surrounding plain is measured. Individual high shapes and clefts cannot be trusted without raw returns.

candidates.nextCheck: Check raw ground returns and aerial imagery for rock or recent disturbance.

cases.visibleGeometry: Several narrow linear cuts converge in a V-like junction near the lower centre. Fine parallel ridges cover the intervening ground, with broader shallow swales on the right.
cases.alternatives: Tracks, field drains, erosion channels, and cultivation could produce the convergence and regular texture.
cases.supportLimits: Measured cells dominate, though many isolated interpolated cells are scattered throughout. The narrow cuts are visible across lighting directions but require raw profiles to characterize.

cases.visibleGeometry: A smooth central swath is bordered by a diagonal break on the left. Scattered isolated rounded highs and rough patches occur mainly on the right; several roughly align near the lower right but form no clear enclosure.
cases.alternatives: Natural boulders or outcrops, vegetation/classification effects, and a track or erosion margin can explain the visible forms.
cases.supportLimits: Central ground is mostly measured. The left break follows an interpolated strip, while some rough patches have additional interpolation; its exact shape is uncertain.

cases.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth surface with shallow swales occupies the available terrain. The lower-left diagonal and upper-left irregular margins abut missing areas. Small rough patches and faint parallel lines occur near the right edge.
cases.alternatives: Natural slope and drainage, cultivation, and vegetation/classification artifacts explain the subtle texture; the straight diagonal margin is a data boundary.
cases.supportLimits: Large black areas are missing terrain. Several rough patches coincide with interpolated clusters; no localized form is reliable enough for a candidate.
